:::{#exm-pearson-angle}
#### A correlation of one half is an angle of sixty degrees

In @exm-pearson-cosine-centered, $r = 1/2$ for $\vx = (1, 2, 3)$, $\vy = (1, 3, 2)$.
By @cor-pearson-angle, the [angle](#def-angle) $\angpar$ between $\cent{\vx} = (-1, 0, 1)$ and $\cent{\vy} = (-1, 1, 0)$ satisfies

$$
\cos\angpar = \frac{1}{2},
$$

so $\angpar = \pi/3$.

:::
